p00-recall-title.text: Warm-up: how far is a point from a line?
p00-recall-title.name: p00-recall-title

p00-recall-q.text: Recall KP01: what is the perpendicular distance from $A$ to this line?
p00-recall-q.name: p00-recall-q

p00-recall-a2.text: The score $1.5$ is not a distance; divide by $\|\mathbf w\|$.
p00-recall-a2.name: p00-recall-a2

p00-recall-cue0.text: Look: compute the distance from $A$ to the line yourself
p00-recall-cue0.name: p00-recall-cue0

p00-recall-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 1 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p00-recall-nav.name: p00-recall-nav

p01-hook-title.text: All three lines separate correctly: which is safest?
p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title

p01-hook-q.text: All three lines separate the classes. Which is safest? Guess first.
p01-hook-q.name: p01-hook-q

p01-hook-def.text: Full margin $W$: width of the road between the nearest points of the two classes. Goal: among separating lines, pick the largest $W$.
p01-hook-def.name: p01-hook-def

p01-hook-cue0.text: Look: three candidate lines, guess the safest
p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0

p01-hook-cue1.text: Look: shade the space from each line to its nearest points
p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1

p01-hook-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 2 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p01-hook-nav.name: p01-hook-nav

p02-scale-title.text: Scale up the coefficients: do the boundary and distance change?
p02-scale-title.name: p02-scale-title

p02-scale-c0.text: $g=\mathbf w^T\mathbf x+b$, $\mathbf w=(1,0)$, $b=0$. Multiply both $\mathbf w$ and $b$ by $2$: does the line move?
p02-scale-c0.name: p02-scale-c0

p02-scale-c1.text: The line stays; both scores double (purple).
p02-scale-c1.name: p02-scale-c1

p02-scale-c4.text: Half width $\gamma=\dfrac{1}{\|\mathbf w\|}$, full width $W=\dfrac{2}{\|\mathbf w\|}$.
p02-scale-c4.name: p02-scale-c4

p02-scale-kp03.text: Note: $\gamma$ here is the half width, not the $\gamma$ of KP03.
p02-scale-kp03.name: p02-scale-kp03

p02-scale-cue0.text: Look: think: does the line move after doubling
p02-scale-cue0.name: p02-scale-cue0

p02-scale-cue2.text: Look: distance is score divided by the length of $\mathbf w$
p02-scale-cue2.name: p02-scale-cue2

p02-scale-cue4.text: Look: purple card: half and full width
p02-scale-cue4.name: p02-scale-cue4

p02-scale-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 3 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p02-scale-nav.name: p02-scale-nav

p03-width-title.text: Road width and the length of $\mathbf w$: when one grows, the other shrinks
p03-width-title.name: p03-width-title

p03-width-q.text: To maximize the width, should $\mathbf w$ get longer or shorter?
p03-width-q.name: p03-width-q

p03-width-p1.text: In words: $\|\mathbf w\|$ is in the denominator; the longer $\mathbf w$, the narrower the road.
p03-width-p1.name: p03-width-p1

p03-width-p2.text: In words: squaring keeps the minimizer and is easier to differentiate.
p03-width-p2.name: p03-width-p2

p03-width-n2.text: Numbers: $0.5 < 1.25 < 2.5$, the same order as $\lVert \mathbf w\rVert$.
p03-width-n2.name: p03-width-n2

p03-width-cue0.text: Look: guess: longer or shorter $\mathbf w$
p03-width-cue0.name: p03-width-cue0

p03-width-cue1.text: Look: blue: length of $\mathbf w$; green: width
p03-width-cue1.name: p03-width-cue1

p03-width-cue4.text: Look: switch to an easier form
p03-width-cue4.name: p03-width-cue4

p03-width-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 4 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p03-width-nav.name: p03-width-nav

p03-constraint-title.text: What do the constraints say? Correct, and outside the road
p03-constraint-title.name: p03-constraint-title

p03-constraint-p3.text: In words: purple is the score $g$ (which side of the line), teal is the label $y$. When correct they share a sign and the product is positive.
p03-constraint-p3.name: p03-constraint-p3

p03-constraint-n3.text: Numbers: point ② $1 \times 1 = 1$ ✓; hypothetical point $(-1) \times 0.5 = -0.5$ ✗, misclassified.
p03-constraint-n3.name: p03-constraint-n3

p03-constraint-p3b.text: We need at least $1$, not just above $0$: points must be outside the purple dashed lines, not on the road.
p03-constraint-p3b.name: p03-constraint-p3b

p03-constraint-f4.text: Primal: $\min\ \tfrac12\|\mathbf w\|^2$, with $y_i(\mathbf w^T\mathbf x_i+b)\ge1$ for every point
p03-constraint-f4.name: p03-constraint-f4

p03-constraint-p4.text: In words: among lines that classify correctly with all points off the road, pick the shortest $\mathbf w$.
p03-constraint-p4.name: p03-constraint-p4

p03-constraint-n4.text: Here: candidate ① has product $1$ at all four points, $\tfrac12\|\mathbf w\|^2=0.5$.
p03-constraint-n4.name: p03-constraint-n4

p03-constraint-cue2.text: Look: numbers: one right, one wrong
p03-constraint-cue2.name: p03-constraint-cue2

p03-constraint-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 5 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p03-constraint-nav.name: p03-constraint-nav

p04-wall-title.text: 1D warm-up: a constraint is a wall that pushes back
p04-wall-title.name: p04-wall-title

p04-wall-tdot2.text: Wall at $-1$: the valley misses the wall
p04-wall-tdot2.name: p04-wall-tdot2

p04-wall-p5.text: In words: $w$ wants to be as small as possible, but a wall stands at $1$.
p04-wall-p5.name: p04-wall-p5

p04-wall-q.text: Where does the lowest point land?
p04-wall-q.name: p04-wall-q

p04-wall-p6.text: In words: the downhill pull (slope $w$) is exactly canceled by the wall push $\alpha$. $\alpha$ is the push coefficient, or multiplier.
p04-wall-p6.name: p04-wall-p6

p04-wall-n6.text: Numbers: the slope is $1$, so the wall pushes $1$.
p04-wall-n6.name: p04-wall-n6

p04-wall-p7.text: In words: a wall pushes but never pulls; no contact, no force.
p04-wall-p7.name: p04-wall-p7

p04-wall-n7.text: Numbers: with the wall at $-1$, the valley is $w = 0$, slope $0$, push $0$.
p04-wall-n7.name: p04-wall-n7

p04-wall-cue1.text: Look: the wall stops the lowest point
p04-wall-cue1.name: p04-wall-cue1

p04-wall-cue3.text: Look: numbers: how hard the wall pushes
p04-wall-cue3.name: p04-wall-cue3

p04-wall-cue4.text: Look: when the wall is not touched
p04-wall-cue4.name: p04-wall-cue4

p04-wall-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 6 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p04-wall-nav.name: p04-wall-nav

p04-lagrange-title.text: Write the wall pushes into the objective: the Lagrangian
p04-lagrange-title.name: p04-lagrange-title

p04-lagrange-f9.text: Set the derivative in $\mathbf w$ to $0$: $\mathbf w=\sum_i\alpha_iy_i\mathbf x_i$
p04-lagrange-f9.name: p04-lagrange-f9

p04-lagrange-p8.text: In words: blue is the original objective; each wall adds push $\alpha \times$ bracket, where the bracket is how far the point is squeezed into the road.
p04-lagrange-p8.name: p04-lagrange-p8

p04-lagrange-n8.text: Numbers: point ① has $y g = 1$, bracket $1 - 1 = 0$: exactly at the wall, adding nothing.
p04-lagrange-n8.name: p04-lagrange-n8

p04-lagrange-p9.text: In words: $\mathbf w$ is built from each point push: size $\alpha$, direction $y \times$ the point position.
p04-lagrange-p9.name: p04-lagrange-p9

p04-lagrange-p10.text: In words: total push of the positive class equals that of the negative class.
p04-lagrange-p10.name: p04-lagrange-p10

p04-lagrange-cue1.text: Look: numbers: point 1 is exactly at the wall
p04-lagrange-cue1.name: p04-lagrange-cue1

p04-lagrange-cue2.text: Look: four pushes chained give $\mathbf w$
p04-lagrange-cue2.name: p04-lagrange-cue2

p04-lagrange-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 7 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p04-lagrange-nav.name: p04-lagrange-nav

p05-dual-title.text: After substituting: only push coefficients remain, and only edge points appear
p05-dual-title.name: p05-dual-title

p05-dual-tr.text: $(y_1g_1,\ldots,y_4g_4)=(1,1,1,1)$: all four points lie on support lines
p05-dual-tr.name: p05-dual-tr

p05-dual-c0.text: $\alpha_i\,(y_ig_i-1)=0$: points with $\alpha_i>0$ must lie on a support line; they are support vectors.
p05-dual-c0.name: p05-dual-c0

p05-dual-c1.text: Into $L$, only $\alpha$ left: $\max\ \sum_i\alpha_i-\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_jy_iy_j\,\mathbf x_i^T\mathbf x_j$ (pushes $\ge0$, balanced)
p05-dual-c1.name: p05-dual-c1

p05-dual-c2.text: Here: $1-\tfrac12=\tfrac12$, equal to the primal $\tfrac12\|\mathbf w\|^2=\tfrac12$.
p05-dual-c2.name: p05-dual-c2

p05-dual-c3.text: Inner products only: $g(\mathbf x)=\sum_i\alpha_iy_i\,\mathbf x_i^T\mathbf x+b$; only support vectors appear.
p05-dual-c3.name: p05-dual-c3

p05-dual-cue0.text: Look: purple card: complementary slackness and support vectors
p05-dual-cue0.name: p05-dual-cue0

p05-dual-cue1.text: Look: purple circles: points on the support lines
p05-dual-cue1.name: p05-dual-cue1

p05-dual-cue3.text: Look: green card: dual value equals primal value
p05-dual-cue3.name: p05-dual-cue3

p05-dual-cue4.text: Look: blue card: prediction uses inner products only
p05-dual-cue4.name: p05-dual-cue4

p05-dual-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 8 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p05-dual-nav.name: p05-dual-nav

p06-nonunique-title.text: One boundary, many sets of push coefficients
p06-nonunique-title.name: p06-nonunique-title

p06-nonunique-c0.text: $\alpha=(t,\ \tfrac12-t,\ t,\ \tfrac12-t)$ with $0\le t\le\tfrac12$ all give $\mathbf w=(1,0)$. We saw $t=\tfrac14$ earlier.
p06-nonunique-c0.name: p06-nonunique-c0

p06-nonunique-c1.text: Your turn: at $t=0$, which points push? What is $\mathbf w$?
p06-nonunique-c1.name: p06-nonunique-c1

p06-nonunique-c2.text:
Only ② and ④, each pushing $\tfrac12$:
$\tfrac12(1,-1)+\tfrac12(1,1)=(1,0)$.
p06-nonunique-c2.name: p06-nonunique-c2

p06-nonunique-c3.text: The boundary is unique; the coefficients are not. $\alpha_i>0$ $\Rightarrow$ on the edge; on the edge does not imply $\alpha_i>0$.
p06-nonunique-c3.name: p06-nonunique-c3

p06-nonunique-cue0.text: Look: a whole family of coefficients
p06-nonunique-cue0.name: p06-nonunique-cue0

p06-nonunique-cue1.text: Look: your turn: when $t$ is zero
p06-nonunique-cue1.name: p06-nonunique-cue1

p06-nonunique-cue3.text: Look: purple card: unique and not unique
p06-nonunique-cue3.name: p06-nonunique-cue3

p06-nonunique-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 9 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p06-nonunique-nav.name: p06-nonunique-nav

p07-myth-title.text: Myth: can non-support points move freely?
p07-myth-title.name: p07-myth-title

p07-myth-c0.text: Myth: "moving a non-support point never affects the model." True?
p07-myth-c0.name: p07-myth-c0

p07-myth-c1.text: Move to $(1.8,1.6)$: $y\,g=1.8\ge1$, still off the road, model unchanged.
p07-myth-c1.name: p07-myth-c1

p07-myth-c2.text: Move to $(0.5,-0.6)$: $y\,g=0.5<1$, the old solution is infeasible and the boundary must be recomputed.
p07-myth-c2.name: p07-myth-c2

p07-myth-c3.text: Correct statement: the old solution stays optimal only if $y_ig_i\ge1$ still holds after the move.
p07-myth-c3.name: p07-myth-c3

p07-myth-cue0.text: Look: decide whether the statement is true
p07-myth-cue0.name: p07-myth-cue0

p07-myth-cue1.text: Look: green: move to the upper right
p07-myth-cue1.name: p07-myth-cue1

p07-myth-cue2.text: Look: red: move onto the road
p07-myth-cue2.name: p07-myth-cue2

p07-myth-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 10 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p07-myth-nav.name: p07-myth-nav

p08-practice-c0.text: New 1D data: positives $3$, $4$, $5$; negatives $-1$, $-2$. Find the boundary, full width $W$ and support vectors.
p08-practice-c0.name: p08-practice-c0

p08-practice-c1.text: Hint: first find the closest pair across the classes.
p08-practice-c1.name: p08-practice-c1

p08-practice-c2.text: Closest pair: $-1$ and $3$ → boundary $x=1$, $W=4$, support vectors $-1$, $3$.
p08-practice-c2.name: p08-practice-c2

p08-practice-c3.text: As coefficients $w=\tfrac12$, $b=-\tfrac12$: $y\,(wx+b)$ is exactly $1$ at $3$ and $-1$, above $1$ elsewhere.
p08-practice-c3.name: p08-practice-c3

p08-practice-cue0.text: Look: find the boundary, $W$ and support vectors yourself
p08-practice-cue0.name: p08-practice-cue0

p08-practice-cue2.text: Look: closest pair, boundary and road
p08-practice-cue2.name: p08-practice-cue2

p08-practice-cue3.text: Look: blue card: coefficients and check
p08-practice-cue3.name: p08-practice-cue3

p08-practice-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 11 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p08-practice-nav.name: p08-practice-nav

p09-exit-c0.text:
(a) Score $3$, $\|\mathbf w\|=2$: how far is the point from the line?
(b) $\|\mathbf w\|=\tfrac12$: what is the full width $W$?
(c) What does $\alpha_i=0$ mean for a point?
p09-exit-c0.name: p09-exit-c0

p09-exit-c1.text:
(a) $1.5$ (KP01)  (b) $4$
(c) It does not push: it is absent from $\mathbf w=\sum_i\alpha_iy_i\mathbf x_i$.
p09-exit-c1.name: p09-exit-c1

p09-exit-c2.text: Next (KP15): when classes cannot be separated, hard constraints have no solution → let each point violate at a cost, called slack.
p09-exit-c2.name: p09-exit-c2

p09-exit-cue0.text: Look: three self-test questions, answer first
p09-exit-cue0.name: p09-exit-cue0

p09-exit-nav.text: Pattern Recognition · Week 3 · KP14 · page 12 of 12 · evidence-first trial · manual play: think at each question stop before advancing
p09-exit-nav.name: p09-exit-nav
